item.title: Daily Update — May 24, 2026
item.description:
In tech, Azeem Azhar's Exponential View makes a sharp case for why AI's biggest scientific value is cross-domain reasoning — finding wormholes between specialized silos — rather than just running more experiments faster, alongside a frank look at AI's creative deflation problem. In the government segment, Georgia's statewide AI program offers a real model for building AI governance rather than just buying tools, plus a brief look at a six-foot teaching robot from the nineteen-seventies. In the grab bag, new research debunks social media as the cause of the vibecession, points to a more specific culprit, and Jerusalem Demsas's essay on penguin disorientation, Spartan collapse, and the cost of choosing stasis.
In this episode: • AI's math breakthrough and its creative limits (Exponential View #575) — Exponential View (Azeem Azhar) • AI Is a Team Sport: Georgia Upskills for AI, Tests Agents — GovTech (via Google Alert) • Where did this early form of artificial intelligence teach kids? — GovTech (via Google Alert) • Social media isn't actually the cause of the vibecession — The Argument • The failure of gamifying education — The Argument • On suicidal penguins — The Argument (Jerusalem Demsas)

item.title: Daily Update — May 23, 2026
item.description:
The AI backlash is going physical: a jar of muddy water at a congressional hearing, Eric Schmidt booed at a commencement — Azeem Azhar explains why facts and promises can't win against a dirty kitchen tap. In government, tech CEOs killed Trump's AI executive order at the last minute, Newsom floated universal basic capital for displaced workers, and states from North Carolina to Denver moved on concrete AI rules. In the grab bag, Noah Smith argues the US debt spiral isn't a future scenario — it's already running.
In this episode: • The AI backlash is the only thing growing faster than AI revenues — Exponential View (Azeem Azhar) • Tech CEOs blocked executive order — WaPo AI & Tech Brief • Trahan-Obernolte preemption negotiations and AI safety community concerns — WaPo AI & Tech Brief • Newsom executive order on universal basic capital and AI job displacement — WaPo AI & Tech Brief • AI is a 'New York story' — for better or worse — Route Fifty • North Carolina senators consider new restrictions on AI in insurance and medical billing — Route Fifty • Denver launches AI platform to boost permitting efficiency and housing development — Route Fifty • America is heading for a debtpocalypse — Noahpinion (Noah Smith)

item.title: Daily Update — May 22, 2026
item.description:
In tech, Anthropic's Code with Claude developer event reveals half the room is shipping AI-written code they haven't read — and engineers are warning of a vibe-coded slop crisis — while Google's Demis Hassabis announces Gemini for Science at the foothills of the singularity. In AI in government, Trump abruptly pulls back on a landmark AI executive order over overregulation fears, exposing a coordination problem at the heart of voluntary AI safety commitments, while California and Mississippi move forward on AI workforce and education policy without waiting for Washington. The grab bag covers Yglesias on why podcasts replaced books as the medium for big ideas, and Eli Lilly's next-generation obesity drug posting twenty-eight percent weight loss in Phase three trials.
In this episode: • Anthropic's Code with Claude showed off coding's future — whether you like it or not — MIT Tech Review: The Download • OpenClaw's engineers warn that a 'vibe-coded slop' crisis is coming — MIT Tech Review: The Download • Google I/O showed how the path for AI-driven science is shifting — MIT Tech Review: The Download • AI & Tech Brief: White House AI order now postponed — WaPo AI & Tech Brief • California Gov. Newsom signs executive order to prepare workforce for AI disruption — Google Alert: AI (statescoop.com) • Mississippi governor launches statewide AI education 'framework' — Google Alert: AI (statescoop.com) • Ideas are still big but books got small — Slow Boring (Matt Yglesias) • Weight Loss Drug Retatrutide Passes Phase 3 Trials — The Dispatch

item.title: Daily Update — May 21, 2026
item.description:
Today's episode covers Google's all-in bet at Google I/O — personal AI agents, a universal shopping cart, and the biggest search redesign in twenty-five years — plus SpaceX's blockbuster IPO filing and an OpenAI math breakthrough. In the government segment: a new White House AI executive order, Colorado walking back its AI regulation law, and an AI name-reader that wrecked graduation for hundreds of students. The grab bag features why immigration enforcement raids are not helping native workers, the surprisingly strong case against the ethanol mandate, and new data showing Chinese citizens are now just as worried about AI displacing jobs as Americans.

item.title: Daily Update — May 20, 2026
item.description:
In tech, Google SVP and labor economist James Manyika makes a data-backed case that AI tasks are automating fast but whole jobs aren't — his "coupled tasks" insight directly challenges the job-apocalypse predictions, and Colossal Biosciences claims a fully artificial eggshell. In AI in government, Andreessen Horowitz becomes the biggest single donor in the twenty twenty-six midterms as the AI industry rewrites campaign finance, while a federal watchdog finds the Agriculture Department running AI systems without required authorization — and Colorado passes a comprehensive AI consumer-rights package. In the grab bag, a bipartisan housing supply bill gets derailed by a fake problem, and the CFTC sues Minnesota over prediction markets while opening an eight-hundred-million-dollar investigation into suspicious oil trades tied to a presidential social media post.
In this episode: • Google's James Manyika is betting that doomers are wrong about AI and jobs — Platformer (Casey Newton) • Colossal Biosciences is growing chickens in a 3D-printed artificial eggshell — MIT Tech Review: The Download • OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy has joined rival lab Anthropic — MIT Tech Review: The Download • Elon Musk has lost his landmark lawsuit against OpenAI — MIT Tech Review: The Download • AI & Tech Brief: The AI Influence Machine — WaPo AI & Tech Brief • Federal AI Spending, Foundation Model Gatekeepers, and More — Brookings TechTank • USDA is using AI — but doesn't have required controls to manage risks, watchdog finds — Google Alert: AI (govexec.com) • These tech regulation laws passed the Colorado Legislature this year — Google Alert: AI (route-fifty.com) • Denver City Council Approves Data Center Moratorium — Google Alert: AI (govtech.com) • We can fix the Trump/Warren build-to-rent ban — Slow Boring (Matt Yglesias) • A New Ebola Outbreak (CFTC sues Minnesota / oil futures investigation) — The Dispatch
